finding: Retrospective series of 152 long COVID patients with pre- and post-infection autonomic testing: sympathetic withdrawal before, parasympathetic excess after, about 50% more autonomic symptoms.
Post-COVID cohort scored lower than controls on delayed verbal memory, attention and executive function with small effects (r about 0.1); 10-20% below 1.5 SD.
Long COVID with cardiopulmonary symptoms had reduced exercise capacity and chronotropic incompetence on CPET with early systemic inflammation markers.
Cytokine network analysis in community paediatric ME/CFS found altered IL-12p70/IL-17A/IFN-g and IL-17A/IL-23 connections versus controls.
Hypothesis review proposing neuroglial dysfunction as a unifying mechanism of PEM and reduced cerebral blood flow.
Conference abstract describing an 8-week combined aerobic and resistance training programme in post-hospital long COVID; no results shown.
Post-COVID subjects had exercise limitation attributed mostly to peripheral muscle (91.7%); severe subgroup had lower percent-predicted peak VO2 (72.2% vs 98.5% mild).
Survey: physical function impaired similarly in post-COVID, fibromyalgia and CFS; pain, fatigue and psychological factors predicted function.
Structured exercise programme in 28 long COVID patients improved CPET, strength and QoL with no adverse effects.
129Xe MRI ventilation defects were greater in post-COVID than never-COVID and related to 6MWD and post-exertional SpO2.
Qualitative interviews on a fatigue-management app.
Japanese clinical overview of ME/CFS diagnosis and treatment.
Meta-analysis: higher post-exercise pain in ME/CFS/FM than controls (Hedges d 0.42), larger at 8-72 h (d 0.71) than 0-2 h (d 0.32).
Japanese short essay summarising ME/CFS diagnosis, treatment and research.
In 136 neuropsychology referrals, fatigue was pervasive (82%) and predicted by apathy, anxiety and executive dysfunction.
Long COVID had reduced global HRV and increased sympathetic modulation versus COVID-free controls.
Citizen-science prioritisation of long COVID research questions.
14-plex cytokine panel with decision-tree classifier separated PASC, ME/CFS and post-vaccine groups with mean F1 0.61, specificity 94%.
note: Preprint; modest F1, no external validation

finding: Long COVID physio-affective symptoms associated with oxidative stress, lower antioxidants and inflammation; about 60% of variance explained by OSTOX/ANTIOX, peak temperature and SpO2.
84% of French association ME/CFS respondents met SEID criteria; 46% favoured the SEID name.
Perspective proposing factors for higher post-COVID fatigue in women.
Serum ATG13 elevated in ME/CFS and induced ROS/NO in microglial cells via RAGE in vitro.
Half of 80 long COVID adults did not reach 85% HRmax on submaximal CPET; older age and shorter time since COVID predicted non-attainment.
ICC ME/CFS had thinner caudal middle frontal gyrus and precuneus, larger amygdala than controls.
Survey: after first COVID vaccine 57.9% reported improved, 17.9% worsened long COVID symptoms.
Five methods of measuring substantial functional reduction gave comparable results; DSQ item most valid.
Post-COVID fatigue prevalence 43.3% in a Missouri single-centre sample; higher in women.
Focus group of occupational therapists on energy management education.
Over 6 months, non-improvers had lower HRV (p=0.032) than improvers; activity patterns incl. pacing did not differ.
12 months after hospitalisation, 27.4% had chronic fatigue and 25.5% suspected CFS; chronic pain in 15.3%.
Case series of manual lymphatic drainage (Perrin technique) reported about 50% reduction in fatigue profile scores.
COMPASS-31 dysautonomia symptoms common in long COVID (GI, secretomotor, orthostatic intolerance domains 74-92%).
Depression severity, not anxiety or PTSD, was associated with cognitive impairment in a post-COVID clinic cohort.
Admission serological biomarkers did not explain post-COVID fatigue and dyspnoea at 6 and 12 months; fatigue prevalence 72.8% then 45.4%.
French memory-clinic patients with post-COVID cognitive complaint showed slowed processing; oxygen requirement in acute phase and white matter lesions associated.
PLS-DA of PBMC and EV miRNA plus EV features classified ME/CFS; Raman of EVs gave AUC 0.71.
CoQ10 400 mg plus selenium 200 ug for 8 weeks improved fatigue severity (p=0.021) and quality of life, with higher antioxidant capacity.
48.7% of 39 men at a Japanese long COVID clinic met late-onset hypogonadism criteria (free testosterone <8.5 pg/mL).
Hippocampal subfield volume differences were found in ICC but not Fukuda ME/CFS versus controls.
Post-COVID fatigue group had lower peak VO2 (19.9 vs 24.4 ml/kg/min, p=0.04) and more psychological burden, otherwise similar cardiopulmonary response.
Socio-political comparison of responses to long COVID and ME/CFS.
Lyme disease raised later ME/CFS diagnosis (adjusted HR 16.95, 5.17-55.60; 17 events) and fatigue consultations.
COVCOG 2: memory, language and executive testing in long COVID versus never infected (results truncated).
COVCOG 1: community long COVID sample versus never-infected; factors predicting symptom persistence and cognitive symptoms (abstract truncated).
MCAM multi-site ramp test: ME/CFS had lower ventilation, breathing frequency, HR and chronotropic response at matched relative intensity, including in fitness-matched subgroup.
No difference in BAFF, anti-CdtB or anti-flagellin antibodies in post-Giardia CFS/IBS versus controls.
Quebec health workers: post-COVID condition at 4 weeks in 46% of non-hospitalised cases; cognitive complaints more common than in test-negative controls.
Singing and breathing retraining pilot improved breathlessness and quality measures; net 9 fewer DSQ-SF ME/CFS cases.
Anosognosia for memory deficits varied by acute severity and related to functional connectivity differences.
Ethnography of a US ME/CFS activist group.
Orthostatic intolerance in 66% on active stand but POTS in only 2% on tilt; OI linked to higher early heart rate.
Severe ME/CFS correlated with plasma EVs bearing CD19 and CD41a, not significant after multiple-comparison correction.
Factor analysis of DSQ found seven symptom domains including PEM; pain not an independent factor.
Scoping review of NIH ME/CFS common data elements for defining long COVID symptoms.
CPET in persistently dyspnoeic long COVID: dysfunctional breathing 29.4%, respiratory limitation 54.9%, O2 delivery/utilisation 15.7%.
Advocacy for Tai Chi as long COVID rehabilitation.
Six-week pulmonary rehabilitation improved 6MWD by 62.9 m, fatigue and QoL.
Post-COVID young adults had higher sympathetic activity (stress index p=0.027) and lower parasympathetic HRV; modulated by BMI and activity.
Prospective cohort: severe GI symptoms at baseline plus low IL-13/IL-5 during IM predicted later severe ME/CFS.
Taiwan registry: TB infection associated with later CFS diagnosis (adjusted HR 1.23, 1.03-1.47).
Systematic review: exercise training after hospital discharge for COVID-19 improved function and quality of life; no meta-analysis.
German narrative review on post-COVID fatigue and ME/CFS, noting pacing recommendations under revision.
10-minute lean test found abnormal response in 60% of 63 patients; hypocapnia most frequent, then orthostatic tachycardia.
Interviews describe wide-ranging, severe pain and lack of effective treatment in children with CFS/ME.
Systematic review of ginseng in CFS found two small studies and low-certainty evidence.
Urinary mycotoxins detected in 92.4% of mould-exposed ME/CFS patients; no control group.
note: No controls; selected for mould exposure

finding: Meta-analysis: deficits in visuospatial immediate memory (g -0.55), reading speed (g -0.82), graphomotor (g -0.59); executive function little affected.
Outpatients with cognitive complaints showed no impaired-range scores on average, with borderline scores correlated with mood and anxiety.
Symptomatic community cases performed less well on exercise testing than controls; recovered participants did not differ from controls.
Narrative on brain fog mechanisms and treatment recommendations.
Athlete screening found myocardial involvement in 2.9% soon after COVID-19.
24-h Holter showed higher SDNN and RMSSD (parasympathetic overtone) in post-COVID versus matched controls.
note: Opposite direction to ME/CFS low HF-HRV

finding: 75% reported generalised pain; fibromyalgia suspected in 40%; PEM assessed by questionnaire.
Meta-analysis of post-COVID fatigue after hospital discharge; abstract missing.
Updated review: little evidence for treating anxiety/depression in paediatric CFS; CBT-type interventions had most evidence.
RMSSD lower in post-COVID (13.9 vs 19.9 ms, p=0.01); OH 13% and POTS 2% prevalence.
Proposes natural-history-of-disease staging framework for ME/CFS research and management.
72.4% of CFS patients had generalised worry; CBT reduced worry.
Female sex, more acute symptoms and neuropsychiatric acute symptoms predicted CFS at 9 months; severity of acute COVID did not.
Abnormal MoCA at 6 months associated with premorbid score and acute respiratory severity.
Review of circadian rhythm disruption in ME/CFS focusing on TGF-beta.
ME/CFS patients with frequent pseudosyncope had larger tilt cerebral blood flow fall (39% vs 25%) than ME/CFS controls.
note: Same Amsterdam group; no healthy control

finding: Fatigue (93%) and depressive signs (81%) more frequent in post-COVID than post-sepsis, independent of acute severity.
Psychiatric and cognitive morbidity 6-9 months after hospitalisation unrelated to acute severity.
Re-analysis of exercise-challenge fMRI: midbrain arousal nuclei activation rose after exercise in ME/CFS, fell in GWI, unchanged in controls.
note: Re-analysis of Washington 2020; criteria not stated

finding: Memory-clinic patients showed slowed action speed linked to acute oxygen requirement and right-sided WMH.
Clinic survey: fatigue 82%, brain fog 67%; exertion triggered exacerbation in 86%; 63% had at least mild cognitive impairment.
Neurocognitive symptoms reported by 93.4%; OI without cognitive symptoms added only 1.7-4.5% to IOM criteria.
Beighton score showed poor agreement (kappa 0.39) with clinical joint laxity assessment in chronic fatigue patients.
Meta-analysis of proportions with fatigue and cognitive impairment 12 weeks or more after COVID-19; inflammatory correlates examined.
Ozone autohemotherapy: females had greater fatigue-score improvement than males.
Pre- and post-pandemic MoCA testing: long COVID cognitive decline improved by 18 months.

n: 10 long COVID, 20 ME/CFS POTS, 20 ME/CFS non-POTS, 10 HC
finding: Long COVID patients had ME/CFS-like symptoms; all developed POTS on tilt; cerebral blood flow and cardiac index fell more than in healthy controls, CBF fall larger in long COVID.
APOE e4 carriership linked to severe COVID-19, perivascular microhaemorrhages (21 autopsies) and higher mental fatigue at 6 months (n=156).
Ozone autohemotherapy: 43.5% went from worst to best fatigue score.
Preprint of the TROPIC orthostatic intolerance study: OI not associated with POTS (13% met criteria on tilt, mostly asymptomatic).
Aggregated methylation datasets found 10,824 differentially methylated genes with small average change; hubs enriched for immune and mitochondrial terms.
Scoping review: brainstem structural and connectivity changes frequently reported in ME/CFS.
Two-day CPET with submaximal warm-up: LF/HF HRV and HR at ventilatory threshold rose on day 2; heart rate recovery differed between groups but with poor sensitivity (63%) and specificity (40%).
Review drawing parallels between heat stroke mechanisms (gut permeability, endotoxaemia, endothelial injury) and ME/CFS.
German review of fatigue in long COVID.
Facebook-group qualitative study of identity in CFS/ME.
Toulouse-Pieron sustained attention was low in about 70% of patients versus controls (p<0.05) despite mostly normal MoCA.
Case report of phrenic nerve palsy found via CPET.
CPET in post-COVID unexplained dyspnoea: 58.5% had peak VO2 below 80% predicted, 88% had ventilatory abnormalities including dysfunctional breathing (26) and hypocapnia.
Sociological analysis of how the 'long COVID' term emerged and comparison with ME/CFS.
Description of the You + ME Registry research platform.
Systematic review of psychological-immunological associations in CFS/ME; executive function linked to IL-1; few longitudinal studies.
ME/CFS had higher IL-17A, FABP-2 and 3-hydroxykynurenine, lower kynurenine and serotonin than controls.
Interviews on school adaptations in Norwegian young people with CFS/ME.
Narrative defending CBT and GET as evidence-based rehabilitation.
IL-2 stimulation and TRPM7 modulation altered NK cytotoxicity in ME/CFS; TRPM7/PIP2 co-localisation examined.
Meta-analysis of moxibustion for CFS found favourable effect versus acupuncture and controls; evidence moderate to very low.
School personnel interviews about adaptations for students with CFS/ME.
Mixed-methods review of fatigue interventions in post-viral syndromes with wide range of effects.
Description of the mapMECFS data portal.
PCASL MRI showed reduced regional cerebral blood flow in limbic regions (ACC, putamen, pallidum, insula) in ME/CFS; ACC hypoperfusion related to severity.
note: Uncorrected voxel threshold p<=0.001 with FWE

finding: Antipituitary antibodies in 56% and antihypothalamic in 33% of women with ME/CFS, with lower ACTH/cortisol and GH/IGF-1 in antibody-high patients.
note: Small; same group as earlier Italian reports

finding: Protocol for systematic review of Tuina for CFS.
Shotgun metagenomics: fewer Faecalibacterium, Roseburia and Eubacterium (butyrate producers) and higher bacterial load in ME/CFS.
note: Largest prospective US stool study at the time; preprint

n: 79 controls plus short-term and long-term cohorts
finding: Reduced microbiome diversity, depleted sphingomyelins, SCFAs and butyrate biosynthesis; dysbiosis stronger in short-term disease, metabolic abnormalities in long-term.
Qigong versus CBT versus healthy control: both treatment groups improved fatigue, sleep and mood, no difference between them.
Salivary Fatigue Biomarker Index differed in severe ME/CFS versus mild ME/CFS and controls.
Preprint of COVCOG 1: predictors of cognitive symptoms in long COVID.

population: long COVID with autoimmune rheumatic disease
finding: tDCS plus treadmill walking improved fatigue and pain over 5 sessions.
Brain fog reported by 7.2%; associated with female sex, respiratory onset symptoms and ICU admission.
In acute COVID-19, pneumonia, low SpO2 and immune markers explained 70% of variance in depressive/CFS-like symptom scores.
Resting EEG source connectivity showed altered cortical autonomic network topology in ME/CFS, related to symptom clusters.
Symptom network analysis: PEM present in 75%, linked to cognitive impairment and fatigue severity.
Work and income stressors associated with worse symptoms over 5 months; healthcare access associated with improvement.
Clustering identified five clinical phenotypes, three combining fibromyalgia with dysautonomia, neuroendocrine or immune features.
Clinical guidance on caring for severe and very severe ME/CFS.
Mesh sling surgery not associated with later autoimmune disease, fibromyalgia or ME (HR 0.89).
note: ME is only a pooled outcome

finding: 7T MRS of anterior cingulate: lower glutathione, total creatine and myo-inositol in CFS; only myo-inositol held with NAA reference.
PLS model: cell-mediated activation, CD38+ T cells, IgM to oxidative epitopes, IgA to LPS, lysozyme and low CoQ10 explain 31.6% of physiosomatic symptom variance; three immune subgroups.
ACT judged acceptable for adolescents with persistent CFS/ME in interviews.
Reduced parasympathetic reactivation after exercise in ME/CFS; resting time-domain autonomic measures normal.
Serum ATG13, p62 and alpha-synuclein elevated in ME/CFS sera, which induced ROS in microglia.
Editorial introducing a ME/CFS special issue and proposing PAPIS term.
Survey of elderly Egyptian women: CFS-like symptoms after COVID related to stress, sleep problems and cognitive impairment.
Diabetic patients with prior COVID-19 had more fatigue than diabetic controls; handgrip comparable overall.
Severe post-COVID fatigue associated with lower anti-spike and anti-nucleocapsid antibody levels (p=0.006 to 0.024).
Online support-group members had severe fatigue at 10 and 23 weeks after onset; mostly women, mixed physical and mental fatigue.
7 months after hospitalisation 61% had fatigue and 55% exertional dyspnoea; risk factors female sex and comorbidity.
Central sensitisation (enhanced temporal summation plus inefficient CPM) in 84% of CFS and 95% of FM, none of controls.
60.3% reported preceding infection; mononucleosis 30%, over 100 different illnesses.
Joint hypermobility (Beighton 4 or more) did not change age at onset, severity or comorbidities.
Hierarchical clustering gave severe, moderate and mild symptom clusters; complement C1q differed between them.
Past-COVID group had higher depression and anhedonia and selective executive attention deficit, most evident 1-4 months after diagnosis.
HHV-6A miR-aU14 inhibits miR-30 processing and triggers reactivation in cell culture.
note: In vitro; ME/CFS only mentioned in implication

finding: Interviews on a coping-focused CBT model for CFS/ME.
Hypothesis piece on mast cells, myeloid cells and nasal-blood-brain barrier routes in PASC and ME/CFS.
Electroacupuncture reduced hippocampal NF-kB and improved cognition in rat CFS stress model.
Enzyme and probiotic supplement 14 days: fatigue resolved in 91% vs 15% on placebo (CFQ-11).
note: Implausible effect size, industry supplement, short, unverified

finding: PASC exertional dyspnoea: peak VO2, anaerobic threshold and VE/VCO2 similar to unexplained dyspnoea comparators; 67% had normal CPET.
note: Retrospective; dyspnoea comparator, not healthy controls

finding: Sex-specific plasma lipid differences: lower PE and hexosylceramides in females, higher HexCer, PI, TG and oxylipins in males.
Audit: 82% of UK hospital doctors believed ME at least partly psychological; little diagnostic knowledge.
Autoantibodies to adrenergic, muscarinic, ETA/B and AT1 receptors correlated with fatigue, pain and cognition mainly in infection-triggered ME/CFS.
note: Correlational; no healthy control comparison in abstract

finding: After about 2 years 65% of adolescents still met ME/CFS criteria; fatigue, pain and QoL remained worse than controls.
DTI: ICC but not Fukuda ME/CFS differed from controls in brainstem and superior longitudinal fasciculus diffusivity.
HLA fine mapping found independent signals in class I (rs4711249) and class II (rs9275582, HLA-DQB1 region) in Norwegian patients.
Patients had higher interoceptive sensibility and trait prediction error but similar accuracy; related to pain, fatigue and anxiety; typhoid challenge crossover.
Routine-care internet CBT (FITNET) achieved outcomes within RCT benchmark intervals.
Review of pharmacological and psychotherapeutic CFS treatments; trials low quality; CBT may help, GET caution.
General pandemic lifestyle survey.
COMPASS-31 median 17.6 (orthostatic, sudomotor, GI domains); OH 13.8%.
Salivary HHV-6B and HHV-7 DNA loads higher in ME/CFS than controls; patients split into fluctuating and stable viral patterns.
Opinion review on the history of the psychological versus biological causation debate.
Hypothesis that hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus overload underlies post-COVID fatigue and PEM.
27% of SARS-CoV-2 survivors had ME/CFS-like features, with worse sleep, fatigue, pain and cognition; serum NfL examined.
Common data elements for GWI research modelled on ME/CFS CDEs.
Systematic review of metabolomic studies in FM and ME/CFS to support iPSC sensor hypothesis.
Meta-analysis of public datasets: lower ACE2 expression and ACE/ACE2 CpG methylation in ME/CFS PBMCs.
72% of patients with persistent polyclonal B-cell lymphocytosis met SEID symptom criteria.
Theoretical model linking CFS to cranial venous outflow obstruction and CSF leak spectrum.
Six years after the Jena Q fever outbreak, CFS rates were identical (3.8% vs 3.8%), no chronic Q fever.
Pooled CFS prevalence 0.77% in Korea and 0.76% in Japan.
Short commentary on physician scepticism despite biological abnormalities.
Survey: PEM among the most frequent symptoms after month 6; 85.9% had relapses triggered by exercise, activity or stress; three symptom clusters.
TRPM3 co-localisation with PIP2 reduced in ME/CFS NK cells after IL-2 priming; PregS and ononetin altered it and cytotoxicity.
Routine bloods showed small differences (higher ESR, WBC, lymphocytes, LDL; lower potassium, creatinine) versus donors.
NK cells from ME/CFS patients taking LDN showed TRPM3-like currents restored, versus earlier TRPM3 impairment.
note: Tiny, no untreated comparison group in abstract

finding: Routine-clinic GET: fatigue scores fell (Chalder -4.7 at follow-up), effects smaller than in RCTs.
Athletes after COVID-19 had normal peak VO2 but lower FEV1.
Perceived stigma mediated link between others' causal attributions and poorer social and functional outcomes.

population: long COVID with and without fatigue
finding: Autonomic NOL index dissociation over time in fatigued long COVID versus controls (p=0.046).
Latvian estimate of undiagnosed ME/CFS burden and post-COVID ME/CFS symptoms.
Herpesvirus serology varied by trigger subgroup; infection-confirmed subgroup had lower CMV seroprevalence, only some associations survived correction.
Commentary on listening to patients with invisible illness.
Parent-child agreement on symptoms and quality of life was variable.
Subcortical volumes: female CFS had smaller left putamen, right caudate and left cerebellar white matter than control women.
Pre-existing migraine linked to more post-COVID symptoms (OR 1.70) and fatigue, not headache.
Network analysis of fatigue, baroreceptor function and aortic stiffness before and after cryotherapy plus stretching; patients showed altered interrelations.
Systematic review: mind-body interventions improved fatigue in 9 of 12 mostly small, low-quality studies.
German patients reported poor access to and satisfaction with medical care; German DSQ-SF validated.
Meta-analysis supports an association between HHV-6 infection and CFS; pooled estimate not given in abstract.
note: Heterogeneous methods; pooled effect absent from abstract

finding: Metabolomics of 888 analytes: decreased plasmalogens (peroxisomal dysfunction), phosphatidylcholines and sphingomyelins in ME/CFS; CDP-choline pathway altered.
note: Preprint of Xiong et al, same cohort as microbiome work

finding: Two long COVID cases with brain fog showed cingulate hypometabolism on FDG-PET.
Preliminary report of the same manual lymphatic drainage case series.
Discourse analysis of patient participation in Dutch Health Council ME/CFS advice.
Headache at COVID onset linked to more post-COVID symptoms, tension-type headache and fatigue (OR 1.55).
Baseline performance validity did not predict CBT outcome in CFS, but low scorers dropped out more.
71.4% had chronic fatigue; 58.7% met PEM thresholds used in ME/CFS (DSQ-PEM).
Protocol-style abstract of a structured exercise programme for post-COVID syndrome.
Analysis of newspaper letters identifying mechanisms of symbolic violence.
Dyspnoeic survivors had lower percent-predicted peak VO2 (77.8 vs 99), higher VE/VCO2 slope and higher PetCO2 pattern suggesting ventilation-perfusion mismatch or hyperventilation.
Critical review arguing psychosomatic hypotheses of MUS/ME/CFS lack empirical support.
13% met IOM SEID criteria 6 months after COVID-19; fatigue 46.9%.
13.7% had new or atypical warning symptoms preceding PEM exacerbation; those patients had lower PEM intensity.
Supplement use 87.5% versus 31.9% in population; higher fat and caffeine intake.
Mindfulness reduced fatigue scores in nurses (occupational fatigue, not ME/CFS).
Letter proposing spa rehabilitation for post-COVID fatigue.
12-month s.c. IgG: 5 of 12 per-protocol completers responded; 4 stopped for adverse events; LDH and sIL-2R suggested as response markers.
Men with ME/CFS showed no HRV differences from controls, unlike women, though HRV correlated with symptoms.
Meta-analysis found no excess self-rated deterioration with GET (RR 0.62, 0.32-1.17) but more follow-up dropouts (RR 1.51).
note: Low GRADE certainty; authors pro-GET; trials used broad CFS definitions

finding: Interviews on occupational disruption in Australian adults.
Kynurenine pathway metabolites differed between CFS, FM and controls; quinolinic acid differed CFS vs FM.
CFS patients with PEM had lower central systolic pressure and higher mental fatigue and sympathovagal balance; none survived FDR correction.
Of 12 post-COVID patients with persistent dyspnoea referred for CPET, 10 had reduced peak VO2; CPET felt to add limited clinical information.
Impedance spectroscopy distinguished oxidatively stressed rat L6 muscle cells.
Herbal pill improved swimming time and immune parameters in a mouse CFS model.
EUROMENE expert consensus on diagnosis, services and care in Europe.
Plasma miR-21, miR-34a, miR-92a, miR-126 and miR-200c jointly increased in ME/CFS; implicated endothelial/Sirt1-eNOS pathways.
Systematic review of PSG/MSLT: slow-wave sleep, AHI, spectral activity and MSLT findings inconsistent across ME/CFS studies.
Theory paper drawing parallels between prolonged ICU endocrine treatments and possible ME/CFS therapies.
55.5% recovered after daily cervical muscle physical therapy during admission; recovery linked to autonomic symptoms.
Long haulers reported falling symptoms over time except worsening neurocognitive symptoms; became less severe than ME/CFS apart from orthostatic domain.
Cerebral blood flow fall on tilt was abnormally high in all ME/CFS irrespective of CPET peak VO2 category, so deconditioning did not explain OI.
Editorial warning about harms of exercise-based rehabilitation in long COVID with ME-like features.
Protocol for moxibustion systematic review.
Three adolescents/young adults developed ME/CFS after COVID-19 with early POTS on stand test, allergy histories and raised histamine in two.
Personal account of extremely severe ME/CFS.
Long COVID studies reported 25 of 29 known ME/CFS symptoms.
Oral minocycline for 42 days: 27% improved performance status by 2 or more; 38% discontinued for nausea or dizziness; benefit greatest early in illness.
Serum exosome-associated mtDNA increased in ME/CFS only after exercise; patient exosomes made microglia release IL-1b.
Autonomic Conditioning Therapy completers had within-group fatigue improvement (-14, CI -27 to -1).
Preprint of ACT acceptability interviews.
EUROMENE report: little scope for primary prevention; organophosphate exposure flagged; secondary prevention preferred.
42% of adolescents with CFS/ME had subclinical or clinical anhedonia; 15% clinical; 72% of those depressed.
Canadian survey: CFS diagnosis associated with female sex, unemployment and comorbid depression, anxiety.
Fatigue common (67.3%) in Chinese nursing students after pandemic.
Recovery rates in paediatric CFS/ME ranged from 4.5% to 83% across 11 differing definitions.
Standard and short CBT improved SF-36 physical function (14.2 points) versus waiting list; fatigue improved with standard CBT.

population: long COVID with fatigue (19 of 42 met CCC)
finding: At 6 months after mild-moderate COVID-19, most had reduced handgrip strength; biomarkers linked to fatigue and PEM severity suggest low-grade inflammation and hypoperfusion.
sCD26 lower only in women; in infection-triggered ME/CFS low sCD26 associated with alpha1-adrenergic and M3 autoantibodies, T-cell activation and IL-1b.
Taiwan registry: peptic ulcer disease cohort had higher CFS incidence (HR 2.01, 1.75-2.30).
16-week individualised activity programme reduced fatigue and raised plasma mitofusins; 51% did not tolerate exercise well.
